truthExplanation.circulatingFraming: Coverage can imply that every AI output now needs a visible label in Europe or that a label proves the labelled content is trustworthy.
truthExplanation.whatHappened: Specified Article 50 transparency obligations began applying on August 2, 2026, with duties varying by system, actor, use, output and exception.
truthExplanation.evidenceEstablishes: The cited regulator and legal records establish the operative date, covered categories, actor-specific duties and a limited transition for certain systems.
truthExplanation.evidenceDoesNotEstablish: They do not establish that every AI use needs the same label, that every unlabelled item is unlawful or human-made, or that a label makes a claim accurate.
truthExplanation.mechanism: The rules add disclosure or machine-readable marking in defined situations so people and systems receive origin context; factual verification remains a separate job.
truthExplanation.realWorldImpact: Readers should expect clearer disclosure in covered situations, while professional deployers still need current guidance for their exact role, system and exception.
truthExplanation.uncertainty: Application depends on facts, exceptions and future implementation; this orientation is not a universal compliance checklist or legal advice.
truthExplanation.headlineRisk: A compressed headline can erase the actor and use distinctions or turn an origin signal into a false truth and compliance guarantee.
truthExplanation.editorialDecision: Publish only the bounded actor-and-use explanation, keep the label-versus-truth distinction prominent and preserve the legal-advice limit.

aidbComparison.rationale: The available AIDB records through August 3 contained no substantive analysis of this exact Article 50 commencement story; LAiDIES therefore used no AIDB interpretation or wording.

claims.claim: Article 50 transparency obligations began applying on 2 August 2026.

The obligations distinguish providers and professional deployers and cover direct AI interaction, machine-readable marking, deepfakes, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation and specified public-interest text.
A limited transition to 2 December 2026 applies to the marking-and-detection obligation for certain systems already on the market before 2 August.
A transparency label provides origin context but does not establish factual accuracy, fairness, safety or legal compliance.
